plant.cvs: 'Charity' – the classic, upright spreading flower spikes · 'Lionel Fortescue' – very upright spikes · 'Buckland' – longer arching spikes
plant.foliage: evergreen; large pinnate leaves with spiny holly-like leaflets, sometimes reddish in cold weather
plant.hardinessNote: Hardy in a cold winter throughout most of the UK, approximately -15 to -10°C.
plant.pollination: not applicable; grown for flowers, berries form without a partner
plant.prune: Little needed. After flowering, cut leggy stems back to a leaf rosette to keep it bushy; old bare plants can be cut back hard in spring.
plant.resilience: Tough, shade-tolerant evergreen that copes with clay and dry shade once established. Flowers in winter when little else does. Pests: occasional mahonia rust and leaf-spot, mostly cosmetic.
